Outlet: GOV.UK (Prime Minister's Office, 10 Downing Street), published 7 November 2026

No one who has served our country should sleep rough on our streets

Key Points
- Prime Minister to write personally to councils in England requesting specific plans to offer accommodation to veterans sleeping rough before Christmas
- Record funding linked to rough sleeping drive creates opportunity to prioritise veteran support, consistent with Armed Forces Covenant commitments
- Veterans sleeping rough urged to contact UK helpline: 0800 9520774
- Government allocates nearly £9 million to housing providers across UK for targeted housing, employment and health support for veterans
- Initiative delivers on Prime Minister's first-day instruction to end rough sleeping

The Prime Minister will establish that national and local government should work together on the principle that no one who has served should sleep on streets.

The Prime Minister's overall rough sleeping commitment includes an additional £874m investment, creating overall record funding of £4.4bn.

Councils will use funding to develop specific plans addressing ex-forces homelessness, working with local organisations and charities.

The Reducing Veteran Homelessness programme allocates £8.7 million to eight organisations across the UK, including Scotland, Liverpool and Kent, to assist veterans with complex needs including health, addiction and employment services.

Prime Minister quote (partial, as returned by fetch): "No one who has served our country should be left to sleep rough on our streets. It is a" principle applied across government, national and local levels.

The helpline has already supported over 1,250 veterans into housing.

Funded organisations: Veteran Housing Scotland; Launchpad; Alabare; The Riverside Group; Wigan Council; RBVE; SSAFA, The Armed Forces Charity; Tom Harrison House
